body.x: INTHETECH (CEO Seung Ho Choun) announced its participation in CES 2025 in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10. The company specializes in developing digital therapeutic devices for cognitive rehabilitation, aiming to optimize technology for better, more human-centered lives.

INTHETECH’s flagship solutions, EYAS, a digital cognitive rehabilitation tool, and COGPLAY, a brain training platform, have gained recognition in domestic and international markets, cementing the company’s reputation in the global digital brain healthcare sector.

Building on this success, INTHETECH plans to showcase EYAS at CES 2025 to reintroduce its capabilities to global audiences. Over the past two years, the company has successfully entered markets in India, Türkiye, Malaysia, Kazakhstan, Australia, Thailand, and Indonesia. Now, it aims to expand its network and secure new customers across even more regions.

EYAS is a digital cognitive rehabilitation solution designed to address conditions such as mild cognitive impairment and ADHD in pre-dementia stages. It offers comprehensive rehabilitation and prevention applications supported by evidence-based cognitive and neuroscience-driven curriculums and training programs.

A key differentiator is the EyeLink system, which combines eye-tracking technology with engaging, evidence-based rehabilitation content. This audiovisual training enhances focus through guided eye movements and maximizes improvements through continuous and repetitive cognitive training.
EYAS also features evidence-based content for six cognitive domains, personalized cognitive data tracking, and a user-friendly interface, ensuring an optimized user and caregiver experience.

In addition, INTHETECH plans to unveil COGPLAY, a home-friendly brain function enhancement platform, at CES 2025. Designed with expert-developed content, COGPLAY is an effective tool for cognitive therapy, improvement, and training outside clinical settings.

An INTHETECH representative stated, “As part of our ongoing global expansion strategy, we aim to showcase EYAS and COGPLAY at CES 2025 to identify new partners and opportunities. We particularly focus on regions such as North America, Malaysia, Australia, Thailand, and Vietnam, where aging populations and rising healthcare costs drive demand for innovative healthcare solutions.”

The representative added, “At post-CES, we plan to stabilize operations in over ten countries, expand global marketing, and ensure that medical facilities worldwide can provide professional care through EYAS while enabling users to continue brain training in everyday life with COGPLAY.”

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
